name: Quevedo-Mashhoon Rotating Deformed Mass
description: The stationary vacuum field of a rotating deformed mass, with independent parameters for rotation and deformation.
convention: We use geometric units $G=c=1$ and the standard Ricci contraction $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Rotation flattens the mass distribution of many stars about their axes. Hernando Quevedo and Bahram Mashhoon found an exact vacuum field for a rotating deformed mass in 1985 [bini2009, quevedomashhoon1985]. The mass $M$, angular momentum per unit mass $a$, and quadrupole parameter $q$ specify that solution [bini2009].¶In geometric units and prolate spheroidal coordinates $(t,x,y,\phi)$, the interval is $ds^2=-f(dt-\omega d\phi)^2+(\sigma^2/f)\{e^{2\gamma}(x^2-y^2)[dx^2/(x^2-1)+dy^2/(1-y^2)]+(x^2-1)(1-y^2)d\phi^2\}$ [bini2009, kurmanov2025qm]. The functions $f$, $\omega$, and $\gamma$ depend on $x$ and $y$, and $\sigma=\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$ with $M>0$ and $|a|<M$ [bini2009]. The parameter $q$ enters those functions and changes the mass quadrupole to $M_2=-Ma^2+2q\sigma^3/15$ [bini2009].¶When $q=0$ the solution is Kerr's rotating vacuum field [bini2009]. When $a=0$ it is the static Erez-Rosen field [bini2009]. As $a$ approaches $M$, the solution approaches extreme Kerr for any $q$ [bini2009]. The equatorial plane $y=0$ is a plane of reflection symmetry, and a geodesic that starts in the plane with no motion across it stays there [bini2009].¶Quevedo and Mashhoon presented charged rotating fields in 1991, including a generalization of Kerr's charged field with infinitely many parameters for axisymmetric deformation [quevedomashhoon1991]. A broader vacuum family includes the Zipoy-Voorhees parameter $\delta$ alongside $M$, $a$, and $q$ [boshkayev2012qm]. The three parameter solution has $\delta=1$, and Kerr's field has $\delta=1$ and $q=0$ [bini2009, boshkayev2012qm]. At $a=0$ and $q=0$ the family becomes the Zipoy-Voorhees field, with mass $M\delta$ and quadrupole $-M^3\delta(\delta^2-1)/3$ [boshkayev2012qm].¶Donato Bini, Andrea Geralico, Orlando Luongo, and Quevedo examined the geometry and particle motion in the three parameter solution in 2009 [bini2009]. They found regions where the axial coordinate circles are timelike, and examined curvature near $x=1$ [bini2009]. Bini and his collaborators calculated the speeds of circular geodesics in both directions on the equatorial plane [bini2009].

related.text: Kerr's rotating vacuum field, with $q=0$ and $\delta=1$ [bini2009, boshkayev2012qm].
Erez and Rosen's static field, with $a=0$ and $\delta=1$ [bini2009].
The static field with $a=0$ and $q=0$, retaining the deformation parameter $\delta$ [boshkayev2012qm].
The exterior field of a slowly rotating, slightly deformed body. A slow rotation and small deformation limit of the broader family agrees after a change of coordinates [bini2009].

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length with $M>0$; the mass at infinity is $M_0=M+\sigma(\delta-1)$
Rotation parameter, a length with $|a|<M$; for $\delta=1$ the angular momentum is $Ma$
Dimensionless deformation parameter; for $\delta=1$ the mass quadrupole is $M_2=-Ma^2+2q\sigma^3/15$
Dimensionless Zipoy-Voorhees parameter; $\delta=1$ selects the three parameter solution
Dimensionless constant $\alpha=-a/(M+\sigma)$, the continuous form of $(\sigma-M)/a$
Dimensionless function $h=e^{2\gamma}=\tfrac14(1+M/\sigma)^2 R(x^2-1)^{-\delta}e^{2\delta^2\chi}$, where $\gamma$ is the source function
